s.g: Any mark that looks like that letter, such as a mark made by a person who cannot read or write in lieu of a signature.

x.f: Alternative spelling of ex (“to delete; to cross out”).

s.g: (originally movie rating) Obscene; adult; pornographic; XXX.
(UK film certificate, dated) Suitable only for those aged sixteen or (later) eighteen years and over.
(sometimes humorous) An unknown or unspecified number of.
(fandom slang) Used between the names of two characters to denote a ship, particularly in anime, manga, and video games.
(music) Used in place of and in artist collaborations.
s.x: Taska Black x DROELOE, Steve Aoki x Lauren Jauregui, etc.

s.g: A ray of short-wavelength electromagnetic radiation usually produced by bombarding a metal target in a vacuum. Used to create images of the internal structure of objects; this is possible because X-rays pass through most objects and can expose photographic film.
s.x: X-rays are light with a wavelength between 0.1 and 10 nm.

s.g: A radiograph: an image made with X-rays.
s.x: The doctor ordered some X-rays of my injured wrist.

s.g: An X-ray machine, a machine for performing radiography.
(chess) A tactical motif where a piece exerts influence or control over a square, piece, or line indirectly through another intervening piece.
(video games) A cheat that allows a user to see other players, enemies and important objects through walls and other barriers.
(transitive, informal) To take a radiograph of; to obtain an image of using X-ray radiation, especially for the purpose of medical diagnostic evaluation.
s.x: Of course there was nothing wrong with my left wrist. They X-rayed the wrong arm!

s.g: (transitive, chess) Of a piece, to exert indirect influence, by either attacking, defending, or controlling an opponent's or friendly piece through an intervening piece along a rank, file, or diagonal.

s.x: I had to put my bags through an X-ray scanner at the airport.
